name: structural-guardrail-composition-template
purpose: Template and executable example for composing structural guardrails around material-risk agent work.

reader_guide.summary: Use this file before material-risk work to list risk surfaces, map each surface to concrete guardrails, and record verification evidence.
how_to_read: Start with task and work_mode to understand what work is being bounded.
Read risk_surfaces to see which security, privacy, cost, publication, deployment, destructive-change, tool, file, permission, or high-stakes-claim risks exist.
Read guardrails to see what is allowed, blocked, and escalated for each risk surface.
Read execution_controls to see composition-wide gates such as human checkpoint, dry run, rollback, privacy audit, grounding, and cost cap.
update_triggers: A new material-risk category is introduced.
A guardrail type becomes repeated enough to standardize.
OpenAI, OWASP, NIST, or internal platform policy changes alter the risk model.
A close-out evaluation finds missing guardrail evidence.

structure_rules.rule: List risk_surfaces before guardrails. A guardrail without a risk surface is not auditable.
structure_rules.reason: Risk-first composition prevents decorative controls that do not cover the actual task risk.

structure_rules.rule: Every guardrail must define allowed_actions, blocked_actions, fallback_or_escalation, and verification_evidence.
structure_rules.reason: A guardrail must be executable and reviewable, not only an instruction phrase.

structure_rules.rule: High-impact or irreversible surfaces need at least one hard guardrail such as permission scope, sandbox, human checkpoint, evaluator, audit, cost cap, or rollback.
structure_rules.reason: Prompt wording alone cannot guarantee security, privacy, publication, cost, or destructive-change safety.

structure_rules.rule: Non-quick work must keep source_provenance and plan_evidence so reviewers can see why each boundary exists.
structure_rules.reason: The platform treats plans as evidence-backed decisions, not internal guesses.

field_guide.meaning: The selected platform work mode; non-quick modes require source and plan evidence.
Risk points that could produce security, privacy, cost, publication, deployment, destructive-change, tool, file, permission, or high-stakes-claim harm.
Structural execution boundaries mapped to risk surfaces.
Composition-wide gates that supplement individual guardrails.
External and internal references used to justify this guardrail design.
Planning evidence that explains why this composition is enough for the task.

task: Publish or execute a material-risk agent task only after structural guardrails are composed.

risk_surfaces.description: The agent may accidentally read, summarize, or publish sensitive local-only files or secrets.
evidence: Sensitive files are routed outside default AI-readable paths by agent-platform/configs/security/sensitive-file-boundary.json.
OWASP LLM06 describes sensitive information disclosure risk in LLM applications.

risk_surfaces.description: A published report or dashboard may include unsupported factual claims.
evidence: Workspace hallucination prevention workflow requires source handles before factual publication.

risk_surfaces.description: An agent with broad tool access may execute actions outside the intended task boundary.
evidence: OWASP LLM08 describes excessive agency risk.
OpenAI Agents SDK documentation separates tool guardrails from agent input and output guardrails.

allowed_actions: Use public repository docs, configs, and generated summaries.
Refer to sensitive-file policy paths without reading sensitive contents.
blocked_actions: Copy environment secrets, webhook tokens, or private files into public docs or artifacts.
guardrails.fallback_or_escalation: Stop the work, record the blocked item in the human decision inbox, and wait for explicit user handling.

allowed_actions: Publish claims with source handles, access dates, and uncertainty notes.
Remove claims that cannot be grounded.
blocked_actions: Use internal memory as the only evidence for external facts.
guardrails.fallback_or_escalation: Remove the claim, mark it as uncertain, or run additional web/source checks before publication.

allowed_actions: Use only tools and paths listed in the task plan.
Run dry-run or read-only commands before side-effect commands when available.
blocked_actions: Run destructive commands without rollback or human checkpoint.
Use broad shell or external tools outside the declared plan.
guardrails.fallback_or_escalation: Switch to dry-run, reduce tool scope, or ask for human arbitration when two valid principles conflict.

source_provenance: OpenAI Agents SDK guardrails documentation checked on 2026-06-02.
OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications checked on 2026-06-02.
plan_evidence: High-impact privacy and tool-agency surfaces use hard guardrails.
Execution controls require human checkpoint, dry-run, rollback, privacy audit, and grounding for this example.
notes: Copy this template into a project or spec folder and replace the example risk surfaces before material-risk work.
Use lightweight guardrails for low/reversible risk; use hard guardrails for high-impact or irreversible risk.
